about: Loader-change rules for modaccel convert, written for this project. Each rule says how one Fabric API use is written on NeoForge, and back. Nothing here was read from other people's mods: every class and member a rule names is checked against the loaders' own published jars by python bench/loader_api.py verify, which records where it found each one in coverage/loader/api.json. A rule's test is its before/after source; modaccel self-test runs every test both ways. Placeholders: $name matches one balanced Java expression; $event is the event object the listener receives; $modbus is the mod's own event bus.

forgeconfigapiport-fabric.ownRepository: Forge Config API Port is published only in its author's own Maven repository

entrypoints.about: fabric.mod.json main entrypoint (ModInitializer.onInitialize) <-> a @Mod class whose constructor runs onInitialize in NeoForge's first RegisterEvent, when every registry is open (GameData.unfreezeData runs before postRegisterEvents), so Registry.register calls work unchanged.

client entrypoint (ClientModInitializer.onInitializeClient, which Fabric runs once Minecraft exists and before its options load) <-> @Mod(dist = Dist.CLIENT) whose constructor runs it in RegisterKeyMappingsEvent at HIGHEST: NeoForge's first client event after Minecraft.instance is set, posted one priority phase at a time (ModLoader.postEvent), so key mappings it adds at normal priority still register.
server entrypoint (DedicatedServerModInitializer.onInitializeServer) <-> @Mod(dist = Dist.DEDICATED_SERVER) that runs it after the main entrypoint, in the first RegisterEvent at LOW priority.

fabric.mod.json <-> META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml: id, version, name, description, authors, license, contact, icon (iconFile from NeoForge 26.2, logoFile before), depends/recommends/suggests/breaks/conflicts <-> required/optional/incompatible/discouraged dependencies with Maven ranges, mixins <-> [[mixins]], access transformers <-> [[accessTransformers]].

fabric-datagen entrypoint (DataGeneratorEntrypoint.onInitializeDataGenerator(FabricDataGenerator)) <-> a method taking NeoForge's GatherDataEvent, called from a GatherDataEvent.Client listener the main @Mod class adds; pack.addProvider(X::new) <-> event.createProvider. Fabric's datagen bases wrap vanilla providers, so each provider class moves onto the vanilla one: FabricModelProvider -> ModelProvider(output, modId) with one registerModels calling generateBlockStateModels and generateItemModels; FabricBlockLootSubProvider -> BlockLootSubProvider over the mod's own blocks, inside a LootTableProvider; FabricRecipeProvider -> RecipeProvider.Runner; FabricAdvancementProvider -> AdvancementSubProvider inside an AdvancementProvider. The Loom datagen run becomes ModDevGradle's clientData run writing to the same folder. For Minecraft 1.21.4 to 26.2, where these providers take a PackOutput; 26.3 changed their constructors.

expressions.about: Fabric's FlammableBlockRegistry.add(block, burn, spread) fills the same two odds vanilla FireBlock.setFlammable(block, igniteOdds, burnOdds) keeps, in that order (Fabric's FireBlockMixin returns the first for getIgniteOdds and the second for getBurnOdds). Forge Config API Port's Fabric API (its ConfigRegistry, which the Fabric bridge mirrors on NeoForge) keeps the config types NeoForge had before 26.1; FancyModLoader 12 renamed them: COMMON, loaded on both sides from the config folder and never synced, is NeoForge's LOCAL. The rule applies where the file registers configs through ConfigRegistry, so a NeoForge mod's own LOCAL configs keep their type on the way to Fabric.

statements.about: Fabric registers default attributes at once; NeoForge collects them in EntityAttributeCreationEvent on the mod bus, which fires after registration.

integrations.about: Mod Menu (com.terraformersmc:modmenu) has no NeoForge build; NeoForge's own mod list opens a mod's config screen through IConfigScreenFactory. The ModMenuApi class keeps its factory as a Function<Screen, Screen>, and the client entry registers it.

bridges.about: For mods written for NeoForge first. NeoForge's registration (DeferredRegister and its holders), event bus (IEventBus, @SubscribeEvent, @EventBusSubscriber, NeoForge.EVENT_BUS), mod container, config (ModConfigSpec, read and written as the same TOML file), play payloads (PayloadRegistrar, PacketDistributor, IPayloadContext) the commonest lifecycle events, and the game events Fabric API has a callback for at the same moment (player log in and out, respawn, clone and dimension change; living death and incoming damage; entity join, level load, unload and tick; datapack sync; item tooltips; key mappings), written for this project on Fabric's API in knowledge/bridges/neoforge-on-fabric and copied into the converted mod beside its first @Mod class. Each class mirrors the NeoForge class named in classes (the members its symbols list), and each event is posted from the Fabric callback that fires at the same moment. @Mod constructors become Fabric entrypoints that receive their IEventBus and ModContainer from the bridge; registration runs at the end of the main entrypoint in the game's registry order, as NeoForge's RegisterEvent does. Capabilities and transfer (Minecraft 26.1 and later; the 1.21.1 layer drops them): NeoForge's capabilities are Fabric API lookups of the same name, so a converted mod's handlers are visible to Fabric mods and theirs to it. Capabilities.Item.BLOCK and ITEM are Fabric's ItemStorage.SIDED and ITEM, Fluid.BLOCK and ITEM are FluidStorage.SIDED and ITEM: a ResourceHandler is a SlottedStorage (one slot per index) and a Storage is a ResourceHandler, the same object again when it comes back; registerBlock/registerBlockEntity/registerEntity/registerItem register lookup providers (asked in registration order, the first non-null winning) and level/entity/stack.getCapability is the lookup's find, through interfaces the bridge's mixins add to Level, Entity and ItemStack (Loom interface injection for the compile). RegisterCapabilitiesEvent is posted after registration. Amounts: items are ints on NeoForge and longs on Fabric (larger Fabric amounts read as Integer.MAX_VALUE); fluids convert at 81 droplets per millibucket, a handler seen from Fabric moves whole millibuckets only (below 81 droplets moves nothing) and a Fabric storage seen from NeoForge reads amounts divided by 81 rounded down (below 81 droplets is not visible) and moves whole millibuckets, retrying a part-millibucket move in a nested transaction. Transactions: NeoForge's Transaction is a Fabric transaction (openRoot = openOuter, open = openNested, depth = nestingDepth, ROOT_CLOSING = OUTER_CLOSING; both nest, both abort on close), and SnapshotJournal keeps NeoForge's snapshot order on Fabric's close callbacks, so the two loaders' handlers share transactions exactly. Energy: Fabric API has none; Energy.BLOCK, ENTITY and ITEM are lookups the bridge creates (neoforge:energy_handler, carrying a Fabric Storage of Unit), seen by mods converted from NeoForge only; so are the entity item and fluid capabilities. Sides: a null direction is the same no-side context on both. Not mirrored: capability proxying, BlockCapabilityCache's invalidation listener (Fabric's cache revalidates itself), invalidateCapabilities (a no-op), ItemAccess.oneByOne, FluidStack and FluidResource templates; FluidType is the fluid itself with its Fabric attributes. The legacy IItemHandler, ItemStackHandler, SlotItemHandler, IEnergyStorage and their helpers (still in NeoForge 26.1) are mirrored as plain classes; IItemHandler.of and IEnergyStorage.of wrap a transfer handler.

layers.about: Minecraft 1.21.1 (an obfuscated game, built with Loom on Mojang's names): the files whose names differ from 26.1's. NeoForge 21.1's registration (ResourceLocation ids, properties passed directly and not given their id, DeferredRegister.DataComponents, DeferredHolder as a plain Holder) Fabric API's networking (PayloadTypeRegistry.playS2C and playC2S, PlayerLookup.world), its world events where 26.1 says level, ServerEntityEvents.ENTITY_LOAD (so EntityJoinLevelEvent cannot be cancelled there), KeyBindingHelper, and its item group events (ItemGroupEvents.MODIFY_ENTRIES_ALL and FabricItemGroupEntries) for BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent. Checked against NeoForge 21.1.250, Fabric API 0.116.18+1.21.1 and Mojang's 1.21.1 mappings.

bridges.about: For mods written for Fabric first: the Fabric API and Fabric Loader classes the code uses that no rule rewrites, written for this project on NeoForge's API with Fabric's names and members, in knowledge/bridges/fabric-on-neoforge (a file at fabric/api/event/Event.java mirrors net.fabricmc.fabric.api.event.Event). convert copies the bridge under the main entrypoint's package (net.fabricmc.X becomes PACKAGE.fabricbridge.X, so converted mods never share a package), points the mirrored imports at it, and each @Mod constructor it writes calls FabricBridge.init(modBus) first, so the bridge can listen for the NeoForge events its Fabric callbacks are posted from. Fabric's events (Event, EventFactory) keep Fabric's phase ordering. FabricLoader reads NeoForge's mod list: a converted mod is found by the Fabric id it keeps (modproperties fabricId), and the entrypoints and custom values of fabric.mod.json are kept in modproperties (fabric.entrypoints.KEY, fabric.custom). The way back points the imports at Fabric's classes again and removes the bridge. Transfer: Fabric API's Transfer API (Storage, StorageView, SlottedStorage, SingleSlotStorage, SingleVariantStorage, ItemVariant, FluidVariant, FluidConstants, FluidVariantAttributes, client FluidVariantRendering), its BlockApiLookup, and Team Reborn Energy's EnergyStorage (whose library the bridge replaces in the build) are written on NeoForge's capabilities and transfer API. BlockApiLookup.get makes a NeoForge BlockCapability; ItemStorage.SIDED, FluidStorage.SIDED and EnergyStorage.SIDED are NeoForge's Capabilities.Item, Fluid and Energy BLOCK, the storage converted to and from ResourceHandler or EnergyHandler, so NeoForge mods see the converted mod's storages and it sees theirs; providers are registered in RegisterCapabilitiesEvent on the mod's bus (fallbacks last, for every block). Amounts: fluid code keeps Fabric's droplets (81000 per bucket); a NeoForge handler reads as millibuckets times 81 and moves whole millibuckets, a converted storage reads to NeoForge as droplets divided by 81 rounded down and moves whole millibuckets (a part-millibucket move is retried for the whole ones in a nested transaction); item and energy amounts are capped at Integer.MAX_VALUE toward NeoForge. Transactions: each Fabric transaction is a NeoForge transaction (openOuter = openRoot, openNested = open, nestingDepth = depth; both nest and abort on close) and SnapshotParticipant is a NeoForge SnapshotJournal; close callbacks of transactions the bridge opened are exact, those added to a NeoForge caller's own transaction are told at its abort or the root commit, and getOpenTransaction cannot reach past it. Sides: a null direction is NeoForge's null context. Not mirrored: ItemStorage.ITEM, FluidStorage.ITEM (ContainerItemContext), entity and item lookups, Team Reborn's ITEM and ENERGY_COMPONENT.
